text: One single menu holds absolutely every setting this entire lesson covers — Refresh, then Schedule refresh, sitting right there on any semantic model's own details page.

Open the workspace, select the semantic model from its content list, and that one menu option is exactly where frequency, credentials, and your gateway connection all live together, in one convenient place.

Turn the schedule itself on, pick either daily or weekly frequency, and add one or more specific time slots. Each individual slot you add counts directly toward the same daily quota Lesson 75 already covered — eight or forty-eight, entirely depending on your capacity.

This particular section shows exactly which gateway, personal or standard, is currently available and online for this specific semantic model. If Lesson 76's gateway installation isn't showing online yet, fix that first — nothing else configured on this entire page matters until it is.
With a personal-mode gateway, you supply the underlying sign-in credentials yourself, just the one time — and they're retained automatically after that very first successful refresh completes.

With a standard, enterprise gateway instead, this whole credentials section shows up grayed out — a gateway administrator has already configured all of that centrally, so there's genuinely nothing left for you to set up here yourself.

One quiet trap worth remembering: if nobody views any report or dashboard built on this semantic model for two full months, Power BI automatically pauses the schedule on its own and emails the owner directly. Lesson 78 covers this trap in full, along with every other way a scheduled refresh can quietly fail on you.
